items.title: Lactobacillus leads healthy flora
items.body:
In 396 women with no symptoms, vaginal bacteria fell into five community types. Four were led by one Lactobacillus species, such as L. crispatus or L. gasseri.

The fifth had fewer lactic acid bacteria and more anaerobes. Making lactic acid looked like the shared job of healthy communities.
items.alt: An open blank notebook, a pencil and a glass of water on a travertine counter
items.evidence_label: Microbiome survey · Ravel et al., PNAS 2011

items.title: Flora shifted in 64 healthy women
items.body:
In a placebo-controlled trial, 64 healthy women took two oral Lactobacillus strains daily for 60 days. On microscopy, 37% moved to normal lactobacilli flora, vs 13% on placebo.

Note what was measured: swabs under a microscope and cultures, not odor or comfort. The women had no symptoms at the start.
items.evidence: Human trial (RCT), FEMS Immunol Med Microbiol 2003

chart.title: Moved to normal lactobacilli flora
chart.source: Reid et al., FEMS Immunol Med Microbiol 2003. 64 healthy women, 60 days, oral GR-1 + RC-14 vs placebo.

items.title: Trials test named strain pairs
items.body:
All three trials here used one strain pair: L. rhamnosus GR-1 plus RC-14. Reid 2003 names RC-14 L. fermentum; Vujic 2013 names it L. reuteri.

The code, not the species, marks the tested strain. A label that lists species names only cannot be matched to these trials.
items.evidence: Strain naming across the trials cited
items.alt: Tortoiseshell reading glasses on a blank ivory card beside a cup of herbal tea

items.title: A larger trial in women with BV
items.body:
In a double-blind trial, 544 women diagnosed with BV or another vaginal infection took the two strains orally for 6 weeks. A cytologist read their swabs.

Balanced flora returned in 61.5% vs 26.9% on placebo. At 12 weeks it was 51.1% vs 20.8%. The abstract reports swabs, not odor or comfort.
items.evidence: Human trial (RCT), Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol 2013

chart.title: 544 women, swabs read by a cytologist
chart.source: Vujic et al., Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol 2013;168:75-79.

items.title: In pregnancy, results were null
items.body:
In a UK trial, pregnant women took the same two strains daily from early pregnancy. BV rates at 18 to 20 weeks did not differ: 15% vs 9% on placebo.

Microbiome makeup did not change either. Pregnant or trying? Talk to your doctor before you start any supplement.
items.alt: A folded knit blanket and a mug of tea on a linen armchair by a window
items.evidence_label: Double-blind RCT · Husain et al., BJOG 2020

items.title: What these trials did not test
items.body:
Every trial here tested capsules of one Lactobacillus strain pair. None tested a gummy or a spore-based probiotic such as Bacillus coagulans.

None of the abstracts reports odor as an outcome; results came from swabs. Not tested is not disproven, but it is not proof either.
items.evidence: Evidence gap, read from the abstracts cited (capsules, swab outcomes)
items.alt: Printed research papers, a pencil and a cup of tea on natural linen
items.evidence_label: Evidence gap · capsule trials, swab outcomes

items.title: Trials tested daily use
items.body:
Every trial above dosed women daily, from 6 weeks up to the rest of pregnancy (see sources). None tested taking it now and then.

So the best format is the one you will actually take every day.

items.alt: A calm travertine kitchen counter with a glass of water and sliced pineapple on linen
items.evidence_label: Design pattern across every trial cited

bridge.title: Convenience is part of consistency
bridge.body:
The trials tested a daily habit, not an occasional one. The practical question is which routine you will keep.

One option: FloraFresh Vaginal Probiotic Gummies, a pineapple-flavored gummy taken as two a day with a meal. Its probiotic is Bacillus coagulans SNZ-1969, not the strains tested above.

Pregnant, taking medication or managing a health condition? Check with your doctor first.
